analysis:
The change in docs/architecture/inference.md is documentation only: the date bump (line 3), the Nemotron Super maximumEncodedBodyBytes statement (head lines ~128-132), and a note on JSON response format combined with tools (head ~530-532). No executable code, keys, attestation, or coordinator/provider protocol surface is modified in the supplied evidence.

Security-relevant claims were checked against the threat model. (1) The encoded-body cap goes from 8 MiB to 40 MiB, and oversized bodies now return `media_too_large` instead of the invalid-media 400. The doc says the charge is taken at ingress before JSON/base64/header inspection (head lines ~82-83) and that the media memory reservation remains. A 40 MiB body per request is bounded by the owner's configured concurrency (default 1, at most 64 plain), so the larger cap affects the availability posture of TB-007 and T-010-style DoS exposure only marginally. The actual enforcement code is not supplied, so I cannot confirm the cap is applied before buffering. The next pass should check NemotronSuperServingPolicy.maximumEncodedBodyBytes and the ingress reservation if the code is part of this PR. (2) The tools plus JSON response format statement means calls are returned when present and only call-free answers are validated as JSON. This is a validation-path semantics change affecting the fail-closed tool and schema validators; the doc only states intent, and the implementation is not in this batch. No prefix-cache, T-041, or cacheScope claims are changed; the doc keeps the coordinator-authenticated scoping and no-receipt statements. No threat-model assumptions are invalidated by this text.

Remaining question: whether the corresponding code changes (body cap, response-format-with-tools behaviour) exist in other batches and preserve ingress reservation and validation.
